From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity vs Hyperscaler options — next tests & timeline

Samira — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap plus proposed next steps so we can align the evaluation with Helios' SLOs and procurement timeline.

Recap (what I heard)
- Primary goal: consistent sub-120ms tail latency for 1k TPS bursty inference on embeddings and 2k daily concurrent gen requests for the search product.
- Constraints: data residency in us-west, SOC2 evidence required, procurement needs a 30–60 day proof-of-concept before reserved commitments.
- Current shortlist: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pools + burst) vs CloudScale managed GPU instances (hyperscaler). You asked for a side-by-side runtime and economic comparison plus an acceptance test we can run with your sample workload.

Attachments sent: helios-eval-map.pdf (mutual action plan), redwood_vs_hyperscaler-matrix.csv (feature/perf/cost matrix).

Proposed next tests (high level) — want to lock these in this week:
1) Throughput & tail-latency run (48h): run your 90th/95th/99th token-latency profile across a representative prompt set. Goal: verify tail latency at target TPS with cold-start and steady-state.
2) Failure & fallback behavior: simulate GPU pool preemption and measure automatic fallback to pinned model variant (must not exceed 250ms extra latency on fallback).
3) Cost/TPU burn comparison: run identical request mix against Reserved Redwood nodes and CloudScale reserved VMs to compare effective per-token cost under your usage curve.
4) Security check: provide SOC2 artifacts and our private deployment checklist for your compliance team.

Who will own what?
- Redwood (Alex): provide the test harness, synthetic load scripts, and a short tutorial on enabling KV-cache and batching profile that mirror your production mixer.
- Helios (Samira): provide the sample prompt set, target SLAs per route, and access window for the test (we recommend a weekend run).
- Redwood (Jordan): lead procurement coordination and follow up on contract/commitment questions.

Suggested timeline
- This week (by Fri 07/02): agree on the exact test window and confirm SOC2/artifact recipients.
- Week of 07/06: run the 48h test and deliver raw metrics + comparison matrix.
- Week of 07/13: review results, iterate on config (quantization/batching), and lock on a reserved capacity proposal.

Quick asks from you now
- Confirm acceptance of the test scope above or suggest edits.
- Share preferred test window (we recommend 07/10–07/12 weekend).

Thanks — I attached a short mutual action plan that maps owners, deliverables, and decision gates. If that looks good I'll schedule the test kickoff and loop in our security contact for the SOC2 handoff.

Best,
Priyom Das

Samira — quick technical note and proposed checklist for the 48h run. I'm the SE who will own the harness. Attaching a minimal load runner script (throughput_test_script.sh) and a step-by-step for enabling Redwood batching/cache flags to match your production mix.

Technical test plan (short):
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west2 (pinned model variant with KV cache enabled). Identical model artifact deployed on CloudScale reserved VM for comparison.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p90/p95/p99 token latency, end-to-end request latency, GPU utilization and per-minute queue lengths, cold-start time, and cost-tracking (GPU-hours + infra).
- Failure simulation: terminate 1 node mid-run to exercise our fallback policy. We'll measure the extra latency and error rate spike.
- Data transfer / egress: estimate bytes and cost for the test.

Acceptance criteria (simple):
- p95 tail latency <= 120ms at sustained 1k TPS and p99 <= 250ms in steady-state.
- Failure recovery: fallback added latency < 250ms 90% of cases.
- Cost: show per-token delta between Dedicated reserved and CloudScale for the same run.

Notes on reserved guarantees: Redwood Dedicated reserved pools are backed by capacity commitments mapped to GPU slots. For procurement language we can provide: "Reserved capacity equates to dedicated GPU slots (N) for the contract term; Redwood guarantees that allocated slots will be available 99.5% monthly, subject to force majeure, with documented automatic fallback to an agreed model variant in case of hardware preemption." Jordan will follow up with formal SLA wording and artifact.

Script attached: throughput_test_script.sh (stub) — this will boot the runner, replay recorded request traces at configurable RPS, and collect our standard telemetry.

I'll prep the harness and can run a dry run Tuesday 07/06 if you'd like to sanity check before the main weekend run.

—Alex
